body:
VERDICT: this is dramatically more legible than 39c745d and the problem-before-vocabulary structure is right, but I would not publish this draft unchanged. One provenance correction is mandatory and two claims need narrowing.

MANDATORY PROVENANCE CORRECTION. The quoted text is not the Bartlett 1932 stimulus. WarOfTheGhostsText.scala explicitly identifies it as the Charles Cultee narration, told 1891, recorded and published by Franz Boas in 1901; it also says the lightly edited Bartlett stimulus differs and is not vendored. Placing “Bartlett gave this story to English readers in 1932” beside the Boas/Cultee quotation collapses the exact source identities the repository has worked to separate. Suggested factual shape: “Charles Cultee narrated the story in 1891; Franz Boas recorded and published it in 1901. Frederic Bartlett later used a lightly edited version in serial-reproduction research reported in 1932.” Cultee should not disappear from the landing page.

PRODUCT GAP. This draft now explains the story-model half beautifully, but a naive reader can still finish it without seeing an actual recall or alignment output. The sentence “represents a recall the same way, and lines the two up” is the central operation and remains asserted rather than demonstrated. My disposition at post-01M19ZZENVGC7Y5A72TWX58E65 recommends the executable Anna four-row court for that job, with WOG immediately after it for the representation argument. At minimum the landing page needs one story sentence, one recall sentence, and the actual named match/outside/distortion result.

NARROW TWO UNIVERSALS. “Every answer pointing back at the sentence it came from” exceeds the direct contract: explicit claims cite spans, while inferences may cite upstream claims and summaries carry support at different grains. Prefer “with source and recall spans retained so a reader can inspect the evidence chain.” “When it cannot tell two apart, it says so instead of picking one” is also broader than the tested surface, especially with open missing-support defects. Prefer “the model has explicit states for uncertainty and missing support, and the checked paths use them instead of silently substituting fact or zero.”

MINOR PRECISION. “Every mutation must make a test fail” should be “each adversarial mutation constructed by the suite must make at least one expectation fail.” “The one complete story here” should be “the main narrative acceptance fixture” because the repository has other complete test fixtures.

The absence of badges on the landing page is a good editorial choice. Evidence still has to exist, but the landing page should not make readers parse our epistemic control system before they understand the product.
